_about.what: Core — one move per object in "moves". The app reads this file directly: save it, reload the page. Every field name is checked, so a typo is reported with the file and move it is in.
_about.add: Copy a move that looks like the new one, paste it into "moves", give it a new id and change every field. Or: node scripts/catalog.js new <file> <id>  — writes a template with placeholder text to replace.
_about.remove: Delete the move's object (and the comma before or after it). Routines built in the app that used it will show it as missing.
_about.check: node scripts/catalog.js check  — or reload the app: a bad file shows the error on screen instead of the exercise list.
_about.names: Anything written as a word instead of an object — "metric": "knee", "template": "lean", "preset": "standing", "conditions": "balance" — is looked up in shared.json. Add reusable pieces there, not here.
_about.notes: Any field starting with "_" is a note for people and is ignored: "_note": "physio wants this re-checked".

fields.id: Unique name, used in links and saved sessions — never change it once the move has been used. Lower-case letters, digits, underscores. Good: "seated_knee_ext". Bad: "Seated Knee Ext", "knee-ext", "1_knee".
fields.name: What the user sees in the list. Good: "Seated knee extension". Bad: a clinical term nobody outside physio uses ("Open-chain terminal extension").
fields.clinicalName: Optional. The term a physio would use, shown in the details panel under the name.
fields.type: "reps" (counted) or "hold" (seconds in position). A stretch held for 30 s is a hold; ten slow raises are reps.
fields.view: "side" or "front" — where the phone stands. Side-on for anything that bends forward/back (knees, hips, spine); front-on for anything that goes out to the side (leg raise to the side, arm raise to the side, knees caving in).
fields.tracking: What the camera can honestly do: "form" (counts AND judges — needs at least one fault with a measurement and a threshold), "reps" (counts only; faults are listed for the person to watch), "none" (nothing to measure — the guide is shown and the set is logged by hand). Bad: "form" on a move whose faults are all words; the file will not load.
fields.vetted: Optional, true/false. true = a physio has recorded and checked this move in the Studio; vetted moves list first.
fields.equipment: List of words: ["none"], ["chair"], ["band", "door anchor"]. Optional extras say so: "ankle weight (optional)".
fields.muscles: { "primary": [...], "secondary": [...] } — plain names ("quadriceps", "gluteus medius"). primary must have at least one.
fields.sided: Only for one-sided moves: { "limb": "leg" | "arm" | "side", "by": "camera" | "pick", "auto": true }. "camera" = the limb nearest the phone is the working one (side-on moves); "pick" = the person chooses (front-on moves); "auto": true = when no side was chosen, watch both and follow the one that moves. Leave the field out for two-sided moves.
fields.upperBody: true when the legs need not be in frame (seated desk moves, shoulder work). Default false.
fields.summary: One line for the list. Good: "Sitting, straighten one knee until the leg is level, hold, and lower." Bad: a paragraph.
fields.setup: Where the phone goes and how to start, in the user's words. Good: "Sit tall on a chair, side-on to the phone, working leg nearest…" Bad: "Standard set-up."
fields.brief: What the coach SAYS out loud as the set begins: the position and the movement in one or two short sentences, no camera talk (the person has already placed the phone). Keep it under about 35 words — it is spoken while they get into position. Good: "Lie on your back, working leg straight. Slide the heel toward your bottom as far as it will go, then slide it back out." Bad: "Stand 2.5 m from the camera at hip height" (set-up, not movement) or a paragraph. Leave it out and the coach says only the name and the target.
fields.why: Why this camera angle can measure this move. Shown to the user; keeps the author honest. Good: "Side-on the knee angle runs from 90° to straight." Bad: left empty.
fields.calibrationPose: Optional. The still position held for the first two seconds of every set, which the coach measures against. Good: "Sitting tall, knee bent to 90°, foot hanging."
fields.camera: { "height": "floor" | "knee" | "hip" | "chest" | "eye", "distance": "2 m", "posture": "standing" | "sitting" | "lying" | "prone" | "sidelying" | "kneeling", "tolerance": 25 }. Leave it out to use the file's default at the top. posture also decides how the stick figure is pinned in place, and how a crooked phone is levelled at calibration (a standing or sitting trunk is upright, a lying one is along the floor; kneeling makes no assumption). tolerance: degrees the person may turn away from the ideal view mid-set before the coach says to turn back; leave it out for the settings.json default. Good: 20–30. Bad: 5 (nobody stands that still) or 60 (the joint is hidden by then).
fields.targets: Optional list of rep counts / hold seconds the bubble cycles through, e.g. [6, 8, 10, 12]. Leave it out for the standard choices in settings.json.
fields.defaultTarget: The one of targets selected to begin with. Must be in the list. Leave it out with targets.
fields.progress: How far through a rep the person is. { "metric": <measurement>, "start": "calibrated" | number, "target": number | "opt:rom" }. "calibrated" = whatever the measurement reads in the start position; "startMin"/"startMax" clamp it (a knee that calibrates at 150° is treated as 160°). target = the reading at a full rep, or with "targetIsDelta": true a change from the start — "delta": -1 when the reading goes DOWN during the rep (a knee angle closing). Only for type "reps" with tracking "form" or "reps". Good: knee angle from calibrated to 172. Bad: start and target the same number.
fields.hold: For type "hold" with tracking on: { "conditions": [ { "metric": <measurement>, "rel": "abs" | "change", "min": n, "max": n } ] } — the hold counts while every condition is met. "change" = relative to the calibrated start. A condition may carry "when": [{ "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }] so it only applies for that option. A named set ("balance") comes from shared.json.
fields.display: Optional. What the live readout shows: { "label": "bend", "unit": "°", "from": "start" } shows the progress measurement as a change from the start ("abs" = the raw reading); for a hold, { "condition": 0, "label": "knee", "aim": "90°" } shows that hold condition. Without it the app shows the raw progress reading.
fields.enterCue: Optional, holds only: what the coach says when the person has been out of position for a few seconds. Good: "Slide down the wall until your knees are at ninety".
fields.faults: What goes wrong, in the order they matter. Each: { "id", "label", "cue" (spoken, ≤ 8 words, what TO do), "tip" (written, why it matters), "severity" 1–3 }. Add "metric", "op" ("<" or ">"), "threshold" and the camera watches for it; leave those out and it is listed for the person to watch. "minP" (0–1) = ignore until this far into the rep; "persist" ms before it is spoken, "cooldown" ms before the same cue may repeat (rules included, so one that is true every rep is not said every rep); "rel": "change" compares to the calibrated start. "when": a list of gates that must all hold for the fault to count — { "option": "variant", "is": "bent" }, { "metric": <measurement>, "op": "<", "threshold": 168 }, "inPosition" or "notInPosition". "phase": "moving" / "rest" (reps) or "any" (a hold fault that must fire while the person is OUT of position; otherwise hold faults only watch the held position). "scale": { "metric": "progress", "times": 0.35 } makes the threshold grow with another reading. Rules instead of a measurement: "rule": "shallow" (rep did not reach the target), "fast" with "minMs", "return" with "threshold" (rep ended above this progress — did not come all the way back). Or "template": "lean" with a "threshold" to reuse one from shared.json. Good cue: "Sit tall". Bad cue: "You are leaning back again" (tells them what is wrong, not what to do).
fields.guide: { "surface": what to stand/lie on, "stop": when to stop, "cannotSee": what the person must check themselves, "regions": [ { "name": "Trunk", "points": [ { "t": "one form point", "tracked": true|false } ] } ] }. tracked: true only when a fault with a measurement actually checks that point — it is shown to the user as "camera watches".
fields.pose: The two-frame stick figure. { "A": start keyframe, "B": end keyframe, "work": { "thigh": 1, "glute": 0.5 } muscles to light up 0–1, "props": [ { "kind": "box" | "bar" | "disc" | "band", "at": "hip" } ], "wall": "behind" | "ahead", "anchor": joint(s) that stay put }. Side-view keyframe angles in degrees: torso (from vertical, + = leaning forward), thigh & shin (from hanging straight down, + = forward), foot (+ = toes up), uarm & farm (arms, + = forward), plus the far limb: thighF, shinF, footF, uarmF, farmF; face: "right" | "left". Front-view: legL, legR, shinL, shinR, armL, armR, foreL, foreR (+ = out to the side), lean, headTilt, squat 0–1. "preset": "standing" | "seated" | "supine" | "prone" | "quadruped" fills the usual values first. Check it on /figures.html.
fields.tempo: Free text. Good: "Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 3 s."
fields.contraindications: When not to do it. Shown as "Do not do this if".
fields.sources: Optional list of { "name", "url" } added to the file's own sources.
fields.band: Optional. "none", "yellow", "red"… = offers the band-colour bubble with that default; true = offers it defaulting to none.
fields.minMs: Optional, reps only: the quickest a rep may take before "Too fast" fires (when the move lists no live fault of its own). Default in settings.json.
fields.options: Advanced: extra bubbles, e.g. a range target { "key": "rom", "label": "Range target", "values": [45, 60, 75, 90], "unit": "°", "default": 90 } referenced from progress.target as "opt:rom".
fields.figure: Advanced: point keyframes captured by the Studio instead of pose angles. Prefer pose.
fields.focus: Advanced: the landmark the live view highlights, e.g. "KNEE". Default: the last point of the progress measurement.
fields.group: Optional. The heading the move is listed under; default = the file's group at the top.
fields.region: Optional. The body region for filtering; default = the file's region.
fields.icon: Optional short label used where an icon is expected. Default "move".
fields.order: Optional. Position in the list; default = the file's order + position in this file.

moves.name: Plank
moves.summary: Straight-line hold with live sag / pike correction.
moves.setup: Camera on the floor, side-on, 2–3 m away. Forearm or straight-arm plank. Whole body in frame.
moves.brief: Forearm or straight-arm plank, body one straight line from head to heels. Hold, without letting the hips sag or pike.
moves.why: The only view where the hip line, shoulder-over-elbow stacking and head position can all be measured at once.

guide.surface: Mat on a firm floor. Camera on the floor, side-on.

points.t: Forearm plank: elbows directly under the shoulders, forearms parallel or hands lightly clasped, palms down or fists. Straight-arm plank: hands directly under the shoulders, fingers spread, elbows soft, not locked.
Press the floor away so the upper back is broad — do not sink between the shoulder blades.
Shoulders stacked over the elbows (or wrists), pulled down away from the ears.
Head in line with the spine; eyes on the floor about 30 cm ahead of the hands. Do not look forward or let the head hang.
One straight line from the shoulder through the hip to the ankle. Squeeze the glutes and tuck the tailbone slightly so the lower back does not sag.
Brace the abdominals as if expecting a poke; ribs drawn down, not flared.
Hips neither sagging toward the floor nor piked up.
Legs straight, knees pulled up (quads on), thighs squeezed together or hip-width apart — both are fine, just be consistent.
On the balls of the feet, heels pushing back. Feet together is harder, hip-width is easier.
Knees-down variant: knees on the mat, shins relaxed, and the same straight line from shoulder through hip to knee.
Slow steady breaths into the sides of the ribs; never hold your breath. Stop the hold when the line breaks rather than when it burns.

guide.stop: Lower-back pain, wrist pain that does not ease on the forearms, or shaking so hard the line cannot be held.

moves.enterCue: Get into your plank — body in one straight line
moves.tempo: Set the line, then breathe evenly.
moves.progression: Longer holds; lift one foot; straight arms.
moves.contraindications: Low-back pain during the hold, or shoulder pain in a straight-arm plank.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.cue: Lift your hips — squeeze your glutes
faults.tip: Tuck the pelvis slightly and brace; sagging loads the lower back.

faults.label: Hips too high
faults.cue: Lower your hips into a straight line
faults.tip: A high pike takes the work out of the core.

faults.label: Knees bending
faults.cue: Straighten your legs — squeeze the thighs
faults.tip: Pull the kneecaps up so the legs are part of the line; bent knees drop the hips.

faults.label: Shoulders not over elbows
faults.cue: Bring your shoulders over your elbows
faults.tip: Stack the shoulder directly above the elbow to protect the shoulder joint.

faults.label: Head dropping
faults.cue: Eyes to the floor ahead — neck long
faults.tip: Keep the head in line with the spine.

moves.name: Dead bug
moves.summary: On your back with arms up and knees over the hips, lower one arm and the opposite leg, then return.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, arms pointing at the ceiling, hips and knees at 90°. Brace, lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, stop before the back arches, return. Alternate.
moves.brief: Lie on your back, arms pointing at the ceiling, hips and knees at 90 degrees. Brace, then lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, stopping before the back arches.
moves.why: From the side the near arm swings from vertical to overhead each rep, which counts. The lower back arching — the fault that matters — is hidden by the floor.
moves.progression: Arm and leg fully straight; a light weight in the hand.
moves.regression: Arm only, or leg only; heel taps.
moves.contraindications: Back pain that increases as the limbs lower.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Lower only as far as the back can stay pressed into the floor; shorter range is fine.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: The exhale keeps the ribs down and the brace on.

guide.cannotSee: The lower back leaving the floor.

points.t: Lowers overhead, straight.
Opposite leg lowers, knee bent or straight.
Pressed into the floor throughout.

moves.name: Plank on the knees
moves.summary: Forearms and knees on the floor, body a straight line from head to knee, hold.
moves.setup: Kneel side-on to the phone at floor level, forearms on the mat, elbows under the shoulders. Walk the knees back until the body is a straight line from shoulder to knee. Brace and hold.
moves.brief: Forearms on the mat, elbows under the shoulders. Walk the knees back until the body is a straight line from shoulder to knee.
moves.why: From the side the hips should sit on the line from shoulder to knee. Sagging below it or piking above it is measured directly.
moves.regression: Hands instead of forearms; shorter holds.
moves.contraindications: Shoulder pain on the forearms; back pain in the hold.

faults.label: Hips sagging
faults.tip: Squeeze the buttocks and draw the stomach in so the hips lift back onto the line.

faults.label: Hips too high
faults.tip: A tent shape rests the abs. Lower the hips until the body is one line.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: A plank you cannot breathe in is a plank held too hard or too long.

faults.label: Head dropping
faults.tip: The neck is part of the line; look a hand-width ahead of the fingers.

faults.label: Hands clasped
faults.tip: Clasping the hands narrows the base and rolls the shoulders in.

guide.surface: A mat under knees and forearms.
guide.cannotSee: How hard the stomach is braced.

points.t: Straight from shoulder to knee — no sag, no pike.
Under the shoulders.

moves.name: Side plank
moves.summary: On one forearm and the side of the feet, lift the hips so the body is a straight line.
moves.setup: Lie on one side facing the phone, forearm on the floor with the elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered. Lift the hips until shoulder, hip and ankle are in line. Hold.
moves.brief: Lie on one side, forearm on the floor with the elbow under the shoulder, feet stacked or staggered. Lift the hips until shoulder, hip and ankle are in line.
moves.why: Facing the phone the body is one line from shoulder to ankle; the hip dropping below it is measured directly.
moves.contraindications: Shoulder pain on the supporting arm.

faults.label: Hips dropping
faults.tip: Push the floor away with the forearm and lift the lower hip until the body is straight.

faults.label: Rolling forward
faults.tip: Stack the shoulders and hips; the top hip should not fall forward.

faults.label: Rolling the chest forward
faults.tip: A side plank that rolls forward becomes a normal plank and the waist stops working.

faults.label: Elbow not under the shoulder
faults.tip: Set the elbow directly below the shoulder to protect the joint.

faults.label: Head dropping
faults.cue: Head in line with the spine
faults.tip: Let the head continue the line of the body rather than hanging toward the floor.

points.t: Shoulder, hip and ankle in one line.
Directly under the shoulder.

moves.name: Bird dog
moves.summary: On hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, hold, return.
moves.setup: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips, side-on to the phone at knee height. Reach the near arm forward and the far leg back until both are level with the back. Hold without the back twisting, then return.
moves.brief: Hands under the shoulders, knees under the hips. Reach the near arm forward and the far leg back until both are level with the back.
moves.why: From the side the reaching arm and the extended leg both approach horizontal, so the timer runs only while both are held up.
moves.progression: Longer holds; draw the elbow and knee together between reps.

faults.label: Hips twisting
faults.tip: Imagine a glass of water on the lower back; the leg lifts only as high as the hips can stay square.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Lift the leg to level with the back, no higher.

faults.label: Lifting the leg too high
faults.cue: Heel no higher than the hip
faults.tip: Above hip height the lower back arches. Reach long behind you instead of high.

points.t: Reaches forward to level.
Extends back to level, not above.
Flat and square throughout.

moves.name: McGill curl-up
moves.summary: One knee bent, hands under the lower back, lift the head and shoulders a few centimetres and hold.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, one knee bent, hands under the natural curve of the lower back. Brace and lift the head and shoulders just off the floor without bending the neck. Hold, lower.
moves.why: The lift is a couple of centimetres and the neck must not flex, which is exactly the detail a phone cannot judge. Logged by hand.

faults.label: Flattening the back
faults.tip: Unlike a crunch, the lower back does not flatten. Only the head and shoulders lift.

faults.label: Chin poking forward
faults.cue: Head and shoulders as one block
faults.tip: The head and shoulders lift together as a block; the neck does not curl.

faults.label: Hands not under the back
faults.tip: The hands keep the lower back in its natural arch — that is what makes this version safe.

faults.label: Lifting too high
faults.cue: Lift just a couple of centimetres
faults.tip: The lift is small on purpose; higher loads the spine without adding much for the abs.

points.t: Lift as one block, barely off the floor.
Curve preserved over the hands.

moves.name: Hollow hold
moves.summary: On your back, press the lower back down and lift the legs and shoulders so the body is a shallow banana.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level. Press the lower back into the floor, lift the straight legs and the shoulders a little, arms by the sides or overhead. Hold.
moves.brief: Lie on your back. Press the lower back into the floor, lift the straight legs and the shoulders a little, arms by the sides or overhead.
moves.why: From the side the legs are held above the floor, so the timer runs while they stay up. The back arching is hidden.
moves.regression: Knees bent, or one leg at a time.
moves.contraindications: Lower back pain in the hold.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Raise the legs higher until the back can stay flat; lower them over weeks.

faults.label: Neck straining
faults.tip: Look at the knees, not the ceiling.

guide.cannotSee: The lower back leaving the floor.

points.t: Straight, held off the floor.
Flat on the floor; shoulders slightly lifted.

moves.name: Pallof press
moves.summary: Band anchored to one side, held at the chest; press it straight out and resist the twist.
moves.setup: Anchor a band at chest height to one side. Stand side-on to the anchor, holding the band at the chest with both hands, feet hip-width. Press the hands straight out in front, hold two seconds, bring them back. Do not let the band turn you.
moves.why: The press moves toward the phone and the twist it resists is invisible. Logged by hand.
moves.tempo: Press 1 s, hold 2 s, return 1 s.
moves.progression: Heavier band; half-kneeling; hold the press longer.
moves.regression: Lighter band; stand closer to the anchor.

faults.label: Turning toward the anchor
faults.tip: Brace before the press; the point is to not move.

faults.label: Leaning away
faults.tip: Leaning away uses body weight instead of the core. Stand tall and let the abs do it.

faults.label: Rushing the press
faults.tip: The hold with the arms out is where the anti-twist work happens.

faults.label: Feet shifting
faults.tip: Shuffling the feet lets the body turn instead of resisting the turn.

guide.cannotSee: The press and the twist it resists.

points.t: Square to the front; no twist, no lean.
Press straight out and return.

moves.name: Bicycle crunch
moves.summary: Hands by the ears, bring one elbow toward the opposite knee as the other leg extends, alternating.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, hands lightly behind the ears, knees lifted. Bring the right elbow toward the left knee while the right leg straightens, then switch sides with control.
moves.why: Legs and elbows cross in front of each other from every angle; the rep count is not reliable. Logged by hand.
moves.tempo: Slow and controlled, 1 s per side.
moves.progression: Slower; legs closer to the floor.
moves.regression: Feet on the floor; one side at a time.

faults.label: Pulling on the head
faults.tip: Hands support the head; they never pull it. Yanking the neck is how people hurt themselves here.

faults.label: Pulling on the neck
faults.cue: Fingertips only, chin off the chest
faults.tip: Fingertips only; turn the chest, not the head.

faults.label: Legs too low
faults.tip: Lower the legs only as far as the lower back stays down.

faults.label: Rushing
faults.tip: Speed lets momentum do the work; two seconds per side.

points.t: Rotates from the ribs; shoulder lifts toward the knee.
Alternate; the straight leg stays off the floor.

moves.name: Double leg lowering
moves.summary: Legs straight up, lower them slowly toward the floor and stop before the back arches.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, side-on to the phone at floor level, legs straight and pointing at the ceiling. Press the back down and lower the legs as far as it stays flat, then lift back up.
moves.brief: Lie on your back, legs straight and pointing at the ceiling. Press the back down and lower the legs as far as it stays flat, then lift back up.
moves.why: From the side the leg angle from the floor drops and returns every rep, which counts. The back arching is hidden.
moves.regression: One leg at a time; knees bent.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Lower back arching
faults.tip: Range is earned; lower only as far as the floor stays under the lower back.

faults.label: Dropping the legs
faults.tip: The lowering is the exercise. Three seconds minimum.

faults.label: Pushing with the hands
faults.tip: Pressing the hands into the floor hides how much the abdominals are really doing.

faults.label: Bending the knees to go lower
faults.tip: Bending the knees to reach the floor cheats the range. Shorten the range instead.

points.t: Straight, lowering together.
Flat on the floor.

moves.name: Superman
moves.summary: Face down, lift the arms and legs a centimetre or two off the floor, hold, lower.
moves.setup: Lie on your front, side-on to the phone at floor level, arms overhead. Lift arms, chest and legs off the floor together, hold two seconds, lower slowly.
moves.brief: Lie on your front, arms overhead. Lift arms, chest and legs off the floor together, hold two seconds, lower slowly.
moves.why: From the side the shoulder line rises against the hip each rep, so reps are counted. Lifting too high is not judged.
moves.tempo: Lift 2 s, hold 2 s, lower 2 s.
moves.progression: Longer holds; add a light hand weight.
moves.regression: Arms only, then legs only — or swap to the bird dog.
moves.contraindications: Any lower-back pain. A full superman puts a lot of compression through the lower back — if your back is irritable, do the bird dog instead, which trains the same muscles for far less load.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Lifting arms and legs high
faults.tip: A big arch loads the lower joints of the spine hard. A centimetre with a long reach is the aim — if your back is irritable, use the bird dog instead.

faults.label: Lifting too high
faults.tip: Higher pinches the lower back; a small lift with a long reach is the aim.

faults.label: Looking up
faults.tip: Lifting the head extends the neck along with the back and adds nothing.

faults.label: Looking up
faults.tip: The head stays in line with the spine.

guide.cannotSee: How high the legs are — the arms hide them.

points.t: Chest and arms lift a little; long reach.
Lift together, knees straight.

moves.name: Supine march
moves.summary: Lying with knees bent, brace and lift one foot off the floor, lower, then the other.
moves.setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, side-on to the phone at floor level. Brace the stomach and lift one foot until the knee is over the hip, lower with control, then the other.
moves.brief: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Brace the stomach and lift one foot until the knee is over the hip, lower with control, then the other.
moves.why: From the side the near thigh rises toward vertical on every lift, so reps are counted. The pelvis rocking is not measured.
moves.progression: Hold the top; progress to dead bug.
moves.contraindications: Back pain as the foot lifts.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Pelvis rocking
faults.tip: Brace before the foot lifts; if the pelvis rocks, lift the foot less.

faults.label: Back arching as the foot lifts
faults.tip: If the back lifts, the leg is going too high or too fast. Smaller and slower.

faults.label: Holding the breath
faults.tip: Exhale on the lift and the brace stays on without straining.

faults.label: Marching quickly
faults.tip: Speed lets momentum swing the leg. Slow marching is what recruits the deep abdominals.

points.t: Knee lifts over the hip, foot relaxed.
Still and level.
